newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN SABENA SEEKS PILOT RELOCATION DEAL BY 1998.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN SABENA SEEKS PILOT RELOCATION DEAL BY 1998.

text.p: Belgian national airline Sabena SA said on Monday it aimed to finalise by January 1998 a deal on relocating its pilots to a foreign country to avoid having to pay heavy Belgian social security levies.

"There are a lot of discussions necessary with ministries, but it is still our goal to introduce it by January 1, 1998," Sabena chief executive officer Paul Reutlinger told a news briefing for British journalists.
Loss-making Sabena said last year that "flagging out" its pilots could save it up to two billion Belgian francs per year.

Reutlinger declined to give details of the negotiations with pilots and ministries. The Belgian state is still a major shareholder in Sabena, 49.5 percent owned by SAirGroup, the holding company which runs Swissair .
"But all those concerned are realising that (the pilots plan) is a very important element for Sabena," he said.
The relocation, known as the 'common crew management' plan, would involve around 500 pilots.

Sabena first considered the relocation of its pilots in 1995 but the plan by then-Sabena chairman Pierre Godfroid to move the pilots to tax-friendly Luxembourg was rejected at the time by Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt.

Asked whether Maystadt, who still is Finance Minister, had changed his mind, Reutlinger said: "Perhaps what we are offering is also different. We would be foolish to be present the same plan presented two years ago."
